subject: general
question: Which one of the following is not a launch vehicle technology?
solution:
The correct answer is__** MSLV.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Launch vehicles or launch systems** are used to **transport spacecraft** from the **Earth's surface into space.**
 
• To establish a sustainable orbit, a **velocity **of roughly** Mach 25 or about 8 km/s** is required.
 
• In **1964** during a test flight, **NASA's largest launch vehicle**, the **Saturn SA-5**, sent a record-breaking **19 tonnes** into orbit. The **first American Gemini flight**, an unpiloted test that made four orbits and was successfully recovered, took place on April 8, 1964.
 
• The development of launch vehicles in** India** began in the early** 1970s.**
 
• In **1980,** the first experimental **Satellite Launch Vehicle (SLV-3)** was built.
 
• In **1992**, an augmented version of this,** ASLV**, was successfully introduced.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Satellite Launch Vehicle-3 (SLV-3):**

 
 
• It was **India’s first **experimental satellite launch vehicle, which was an all solid, **four-stage vehicle **weighing 17 tonnes.
 
• It had a** height of 22m **and it was capable of placing **40 kg class** payloads in** Low Earth Orbit (LEO).**
 
• The flight of SLV3, launch on **July 18, 1980,** from** Sriharikota Range (SHAR),** successfully placed** Rohini satellite, RS-1**, into orbit, thereby making** India** the** sixth member** of an exclusive club of **space-faring.**
 
 
 
• **Augmented Satellite Launch Vehicle (ASLV)**:
 
 
• The Augmented Satellite Launch Spacecraft (ASLV) was created as a** low-cost intermediate vehicle** for demonstrating and validating key technologies. 
 
• The **23.8 m tall** ASLV was constructed as a **five-stage, all-solid propellant vehicle** with a mission of orbiting **150 kg class **satellites into 400 km circular orbits, with a lift-off weight of 40 tonnes.
 
• **Four developmental flights **were carried out as part of the ASLV programme:
 

 
 
• On **March 24, 1987**, the first developmental flight took place.
 
• The second was on **July 13, 1989.**
 
• On** May 20, 1992**, ASLV-D3 was successfully launched, with SROSS-C (106 kg) being placed into a 255 x 430 km orbit.
 
• On** May 4, 1994**, ASLV-D4 orbited SROSS-C2, a 106-kilogram satellite. It operated for seven years and carried two payloads: the **Gamma-Ray Burst (GRB) Experiment** and the **Retarding Potential Analyzer (RPA).**
 
 
 
• **Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV):**
 
 
• India's **third-generation launch vehicle **is the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV).
 
• It is the** nation's first** launch vehicle to have **liquid stages.**
 
• PSLV features** four stages** that cycle between **solid and liquid propulsion** technologies.
 
• PSLV's first successful launch was in** October 1994**, with **39 successful missions** in a row by **June 2017.**
 
• Between **1994 and 2017**, the vehicle launched **48 Indian spacecraft and 209 satellites** for international customers.
 
• The vehicle was successful in launching two spacecraft —** Chandrayaan-1 in 2008 **and **Mars Orbiter Spacecraft in 2013 **– to the Moon and Mars, respectively.
 
• PSLV has acquired the nickname** "ISRO's workhorse" **for delivering various satellites to Low Earth Orbits, particularly the IRS series of satellites.
 
 
 
• **Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV):**
 
 
• It is capable of launching **2-tonne satellites** into **Geosynchronous Transfer Orbi**t, such as the INSAT and GSAT series of communication satellites (GTO).
 
• The** Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle Mark-II (GSLV Mk II)** is **India's largest **and currently operational launch vehicle.
 
• The GSLV Mk-II is a** fourth-generation** launch vehicle capable of launching satellites with a lift-off mass of up to 2,500 kg to the GTO and up to 5,000 kg to the LEO.
